body:
`AnalyticDoubleBarrierEngine` never reads `arguments_.rebate`, so a non-zero rebate is silently ignored. For a 100-strike call with barriers 80/130, rebate 3, 25% volatility and 180 days, it returns 3.544 for the knock-out and 4.139 for the knock-in, while `BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine` gives 4.567 and 6.051.

This PR adds the rebate using the same convention as the lattice and Monte Carlo engines:

* for knock-outs it is paid at the first hit of either barrier, which is the sum of the KIKO and KOKI binaries priced by `AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine`;
* for knock-ins it is paid at expiry if no barrier is hit, which is the knock-out (double no-touch) binary.

The binaries use the option strike, so that they pick the same volatility as the option when there's a smile.

With the fix the engine returns 4.562 and 6.056. The rebate value agrees with the lattice engine to about 0.4%, and the remaining difference has the sign expected from the lattice's discrete barrier monitoring (it misses some hits, so it slightly underprices the knock-out rebate and overprices the knock-in one). The code only runs for a non-zero rebate, so existing results are unchanged.

The quanto engine, which passes the rebate through to this engine, now includes it as well. `VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine` now rejects a non-zero rebate, since its smile adjustment and in-out parity don't account for it yet; proper support can follow in a separate PR.

**Tests:** `testAnalyticRebate` checks both rebate values against `BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine`, checks that with zero rates the knock-out and knock-in rebates add up to the rebate itself, and checks that with a volatility smile the price matches a flat volatility equal to the smile at the option strike. `testVannaVolgaRejectsRebate` checks that the vanna-volga engine throws for a non-zero rebate and still prices without one. Both fail on master and pass with this change.

comments.body:
I've let an AI reviewer loose on your PR.  Here's the oracle:

---

The description says the vanna-volga and quanto engines "now include [the rebate] as well". That holds for knock-outs. For knock-ins in VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine the result is now wrong.

**Cause**. vannavolgadoublebarrierengine.hpp always prices a knock-out with the Black-Scholes engine, passing arguments_.rebate (lines ~187-189). It smile-adjusts that price and caps it to [0, vanilla]. For a knock-in it then uses parity (line ~392):

inPrice = vanillaOption - outPrice;

Before this PR the BS engine ignored the rebate, so outPrice was rebate-free and parity was consistent. Now outPrice includes the at-hit knock-out rebate.

**Effect**. Let KO₀ and KI₀ be the prices without a rebate, so vanilla = KO₀ + KI₀. Let A be the value of the at-hit rebate (KIKO + KOKI) and N the value of the expiry rebate (double no-touch).

- Correct knock-in with rebate: KI₀ + N.
- Vanna-volga now: vanilla − (KO₀ + A) = KI₀ − A.

The knock-in subtracts a rebate it never pays and omits the one it does pay. The error is −(A + N), roughly the full rebate times the discount factor. So adding a rebate now makes the vanna-volga knock-in cheaper, which is the wrong direction.

**Other effects on the knock-out path**:

- The cap min(vanillaOption, outPrice) assumes a knock-out can't exceed the vanilla. With a rebate it can, for example with a large rebate on an out-of-the-money option. The result is then silently clipped.

---

Back to a human comment.  Given that fixing the Vanna-Volga engine might not be trivial, for the time being we might be better off adding a QL_REQUIRE to it that checks that the rebate is 0.  This PR might then be merged, and a proper treatment of the rebate for Vanna-Volga left for later.

Ha, the oracle has spoken, and it’s right on both counts! I’ve pushed the fixes: the rebate now uses the option strike, and the vanna-volga engine rejects non-zero rebates with a QL_REQUIRE, with tests for both. I’ve also corrected the description, which overstated what the vanna-volga engine does. Happy to look into proper rebate support for vanna-volga as a follow-up PR once this one is in.

review_comments.body: We should use the actual option strike here, so that we pick the correct volatility in case there's a smile.

Done! With a strike-dependent surface the old version actually threw, since strike 0 was outside the surface’s range, so good catch. The test now checks that the price with a smile matches a flat vol equal to the smile at the option strike.

title: Add rebates to the analytic double-barrier engine
